Part 0 · Practice set

Practice set: toolkit

Twenty-five questions across the eight toolkit chapters, to attempt without notes

This practice set mixes algebra and functions, discrete maths and logic, vectors and matrices, slopes and gradients, probability and statistics, charts and tables, Python and algorithms, and two logic puzzles. Attempt it without notes and with the chapters closed. A timer is there if you want the pressure of a clock, and about 45 minutes is a fair target.

When you press Score my answers at the end, the page shows your score by area and the questions you missed, with links to the sections to revise. It does not show the correct answers. Revise the sections the score points to, try the missed questions again, and attempt the whole set again after a week.

You will need: a pen, paper and a calculator, and what the toolkit chapters teach: 0.1 Python, 0.2 Algorithms, 0.3 Algebra and functions, 0.4 Discrete maths and logic, 0.5 Vectors and matrices, 0.6 Slopes and gradients, 0.7 Probability and statistics and 0.8 Reading charts and tables.

How to use this set

  • Close the chapters. Keep a pen, paper and a calculator beside you.
  • Choose a time and press Start timer when you begin. Pause it when you leave. The clock counts down, then goes on counting past zero so that you can see how long you took. The timer is optional.
  • Skip a question and return to it if you like. Your answers are saved in this browser as you type.
  • Press Score my answers at the end. The set is scored only then.
Time allowed

Your answers and the timer are saved in this browser only. No data is sent anywhere.

Algebra and functions

Question 1Algebra and functions

In murky water off Juhu, the light at a depth of \(d\) metres is \(0.7^{d}\) times the light at the surface. These numbers are made up. What is the smallest whole number of metres at which less than 10% of the surface light is left?

Revise 0.3 Logarithms and 0.3 Exponents.

Question 2Algebra and functions

The left graph shows a function \(f\) and the right graph shows a function \(g\). The dots mark whole-number inputs. What is \(g(f(0))\)?

Choose one answer

Revise 0.3 Composition and 0.3 Functions as machines.

Discrete maths and logic

Question 3Discrete maths and logic

Mumbai AI Lab sends a team of three to the Juhu rock pool, chosen from 8 students. One of the three is the diver. The other two are note-takers, who do the same job, so their order does not matter. In how many different ways can the team be chosen?

Revise 0.4 Counting orders and groups.

Question 4Discrete maths and logic

A dive log has 60 frames (made-up numbers). A bamboo shark appears in 25 frames and a hammerhead appears in 18 frames. Both appear together in 9 frames. In how many frames does neither shark appear?

Revise 0.4 Sets and Venn diagrams.

Question 5Discrete maths and logic

The SharkCam alarm rings when a fin is seen (\(A\)). It also rings when a ping is heard (\(B\)) and the battery is not low (\(C\) is false). In symbols the rule is \(A\) OR (\(B\) AND NOT \(C\)). The three inputs can be true or false, which gives 8 rows in the truth table. For how many of the 8 rows does the alarm ring?

Choose one answer

Revise 0.4 Logic and truth tables.

Vectors and matrices

Question 6Vectors and matrices

Two readings from the SharkCam sensor are the vectors \(\mathbf{u} = (3,\ k,\ -2)\) and \(\mathbf{v} = (4,\ 5,\ k)\). For which value of \(k\) are \(\mathbf{u}\) and \(\mathbf{v}\) perpendicular?

Revise 0.5 Length, angle and cosine similarity and 0.5 The dot product.

Question 7Vectors and matrices

Let \(A = \begin{pmatrix}1&0&2\\0&3&1\end{pmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&1\\3&0\end{pmatrix}\). Which of these is the matrix product \(AB\)?

Choose one answer

Revise 0.5 Matrix products and transposes.

Question 8Vectors and matrices

The matrix \(M = \begin{pmatrix}2&3\\4&1\end{pmatrix}\) moves all points of the plane. A triangle of area 5 is moved with them. What is the area of the new triangle?

Revise 0.5 A matrix bends the plane.

Question 9Vectors and matrices

Let \(A = \begin{pmatrix}5&2\\2&2\end{pmatrix}\). Which of these vectors is stretched by \(A\) without being turned, so that \(A\mathbf{v}\) lies along \(\mathbf{v}\)?

Choose one answer

Revise 0.5 Eigenvectors.

Slopes and gradients

Question 10Slopes and gradients

During training, a loss is \(L(w) = 3w^{2} - \ln w\) for \(w > 0\). What is the slope of \(L\) at \(w = 0.25\)?

Revise 0.6 The slopes this primer uses and 0.6 Slope as sensitivity.

Question 11Slopes and gradients

A SharkCam neuron turns a measurement \(x\) into a score \(z = 0.4x - 2\). It then turns the score into an output \(a = \sigma(z)\), with \(\sigma(z) = 1/(1+e^{-z})\). The loss is \(\ell = (a-1)^2\). What is \(d\ell/dx\) at \(x = 5\)?

Revise 0.6 The chain rule and 0.6 The slopes this primer uses.

Question 12Slopes and gradients

A loss depends on two weights: \(L(w_1, w_2) = w_1^{2} + 3w_1w_2 + 2w_2^{2}\). Gradient descent starts at \((w_1, w_2) = (1, 2)\) with learning rate \(\eta = 0.1\). After one step, what is the new value of \(w_2\)?

Revise 0.6 The gradient and 0.6 Partial derivatives.

Probability and statistics

Question 13Probability and statistics

A clinic in Mumbai screens women for a condition that 2% of them have. The numbers are invented for this question. The screening test flags 95% of the women who have the condition. It also flags 10% of the women who do not have it. Of the women the test flags, about what percentage actually have the condition? Give a whole number.

Revise 0.7 Base rates and Bayes' rule.

Question 14Probability and statistics

Five spadenose sharks measure 34, 38, 40, 42 and 46 cm (made-up lengths). Find the standard deviation of the five lengths, dividing the sum of the squared deviations by 5.

Revise 0.7 Mean and spread.

Question 15Probability and statistics

SharkCam's detector B scores higher than detector A on the same 200 held-out frames. A paired comparison of the two gives a p-value of 0.03. Which statement is correct?

Choose one answer

Revise 0.7 Is model B better than model A?.

Question 16Probability and statistics

Across 30 Mumbai beaches, the beaches with more lifeguards also report more shark sightings (correlation \(r = 0.7\); made-up numbers). A councillor proposes removing lifeguards to cut sightings. Which is the strongest reason the plan may fail?

Choose one answer

Revise 0.7 Correlation and causation.

Python and algorithms

Question 20Python and algorithms

What does this program print?

dives = [4, 1, 3]
same = dives
same.append(dives[0] + dives[2])
r = {}
for n in same:
    r[n % 3] = r.get(n % 3, 0) + n
print(len(dives), r[1])
Choose one answer

Revise 0.1 Lists and loops, 0.1 Dictionaries, tuples and sets and 0.2 Tracing code by hand.

Question 21Python and algorithms

This code counts the pairs of frames that look alike. With \(n = 1{,}000\) frames it takes 3 seconds. About how long will it take with \(n = 2{,}000\) frames?

close = 0
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(i + 1, n):
        if dist(f[i], f[j]) < 5:
            close += 1
Choose one answer

Revise 0.2 Big-O: steps against size.

Question 22Python and algorithms

Trace this binary search by hand. What does the program print?

lengths = [18, 24, 29, 33, 38, 41,
           45, 47, 52, 58, 63]
lo, hi, steps = 0, 10, 0
while lo <= hi:
    mid = (lo + hi) // 2
    steps += 1
    if lengths[mid] == 47:
        break
    elif lengths[mid] < 47:
        lo = mid + 1
    else:
        hi = mid - 1
print(steps)

Revise 0.2 Linear and binary search and 0.2 Tracing code by hand.

Question 23Python and algorithms

This insertion sort counts its comparisons. What does the program print?

a = [52, 38, 61, 29, 44]
count = 0
for i in range(1, len(a)):
    j = i
    while j > 0:
        count += 1
        if a[j - 1] > a[j]:
            t = a[j]
            a[j] = a[j - 1]
            a[j - 1] = t
            j -= 1
        else:
            break
print(count)

Revise 0.2 Sorting: insertion and merge and 0.2 Tracing code by hand.

Logic puzzles

Question 24Logic puzzles

Four students, Asha, Bilal, Chitra and Dev, were at Juhu. Someone left the lens cap on SharkCam, and the dive footage came out black. Only one of the four did it. They said:

  • Asha: “Bilal did it.”
  • Bilal: “Dev did it.”
  • Chitra: “I did not do it.”
  • Dev: “Bilal is wrong.”

Only one of the four statements is true. Who left the lens cap on?

Choose one answer

Revise 0.4 Logic and truth tables.

Question 25Logic puzzles

Before a dive, six jobs are done one at a time. An arrow from one job to another means the first must be finished before the second can start. The jobs are charge the battery, seal the housing, set the clock, launch, sync the depth log and record. In how many different orders can the six jobs be done?

Revise 0.4 Graphs, trees and DAGs and 0.4 Counting orders and groups.

Finish and score

Press the button when you are done. Blank answers count as missed. The page then locks your answers, shows your score by area and links to the sections to revise. It does not show the correct answers.

Where the numbers come from

  1. Questions 17, 18 and 19 use the made-up SharkCam catch table: 600 records generated from published length-weight relationships, not field data (primer/data/sharks/catch.csv). The monthly counts in question 17 are from the table. The table in question 18 comes from a decision tree of depth 2 on length, scored with five-fold cross-validation (shuffled folds, seed 4127). The table in question 19 comes from spadenose records only, five-fold cross-validation repeated with seeds 1 to 5, using scikit-learn. The script is data/make_tables.py.
  2. The numbers in the other questions, including the clinic, the beaches and the dive log, are invented for practice.
  3. The ideas come from the toolkit chapters listed at the top of this page. The lie factor in question 17 is the one defined in 0.8, after Edward Tufte.
